To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sharing economy has been a disruptive innovation that has been received differently in different places and that the sharing economy needs to be better integrated with existing tourism ecosystems in order to realise its potential.

(1) the sharing economy has transformed and disrupted the tourism sector, (2) different destinations have featured different levels of receptivity towards sharing economy organisations, (3) governance structures have influenced how sharing economy organisations operate, (4) there is an urgent to re align existing legislations and business models in the tourism sector.
the sharing economy has transformed tourism, though governance structures have influenced the extent of receptivity within Australia and Singapore.

the sharing economy in the context of tourism, and the impact of the sharing economy on tourism.
how tourism organisations can be more proactive in terms of embracing the sharing economy.
how tourism organisations can better respond to the sharing economy, and in particular AirBnB, and Uber.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sharing economy is here to stay.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sharing economy is not just about sharing but about the ability to create value through the sharing of assets.
the sharing economy is not just a new form of tourism, it is also a new form of business and governance.
the sharing economy can only flourish when the government and the private sector work in tandem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sharing economy has the potential to transform tourism, however, the extent of its success depends on the receptiveness of the host destination.
tourism stakeholders must work together to create a smart tourism ecosystem that is conducive for the sharing economy to flourish.

tourism organisations should not only focus on the sharing economy as a means to generate additional revenue, but also to create a more inclusive environment where tourists are able to interact with locals and experience the destination in a more authentic and sustainable way.
